Friday 09 October 2026 · 26 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 fell 1.64% to 22,232 and decliners led 2,251 to 299
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned -0.73% weighted by turnover, against -2.44% for the median stock, a gap of 1.7 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Senco Gold Limited rose 5.2% on 52 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Gold prices rise Rs 1,500/10g; silver up Rs 3,100/kg ahead of US economic data, softer yields. Buy, sell or hold?”.

PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery Limited rose 11.2% on 103 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Diamond Power Infrastructure among 3 stocks that closed above VWAP”.

Fino Payments Bank Limited rose 13.0% on 94 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “GST 2026: Simpler compliance, tech-led enforcement reflect growing trust between government and industry, says Deloitte’s MS Mani”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in Indokem Limited (169x), Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (87x), Brooks Laboratories Limited (61x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

Oil falls as Trump comments on Iran talks ease supply concerns
Brent crude prices dropped after remarks by Donald Trump pointed toward possible diplomatic engagement with Iran, unwinding geopolitical supply premiums. Cheaper crude eases imported inflation, supports the rupee, and lowers input costs for paint makers, tyre manufacturers, and specialty chemicals. State-run refiners like IOC and BPCL also gain room on retail fuel marketing margins.

India IT set for fourth year of weak growth on geopolitics, AI risks
Tata Consultancy Services delivered sequential revenue growth of just 0.5% in constant-currency terms, setting a muted benchmark before HCL Technologies and Tech Mahindra report earnings. Prolonged weakness in US banking and retail discretionary budgets continues to cap dollar revenue growth across Tier-1 IT services. With sector valuations still near historical averages, margin expansion now depends entirely on cost rationalisation rather than volume recovery.

Reducing filing friction and automated scrutiny lowers administrative overhead and frees up working capital across distributor networks. Organised consumer goods, auto component makers, and third-party logistics firms benefit directly as their unorganised vendor ecosystems face lower compliance hurdles.

Govt likely to finalise critical minerals stockpiling policy in a month
The Mines Ministry plans to finalise a strategic stockpiling policy within a month, establishing four dedicated reserves for lithium, cobalt, and rare earths. By absorbing global price shocks and supply disruptions, a state buffer protects input costs and gross margins for domestic electronics manufacturers like Dixon Technologies and battery producers like Exide. Cabinet approval details on funding mechanisms will confirm the operational scale.

Global Market: Singapore likely to tighten monetary policy as growth and inflation risks mount
The Monetary Authority of Singapore is expected to steepen the slope of its currency band to contain persistent core inflation and rising energy import costs. A stronger Singapore dollar exerts mild depreciation pressure on the rupee across bilateral trade settlements, while tighter regional liquidity marginally increases borrowing costs for Indian corporates accessing foreign currency loans in Singapore.

Thermax share price soars 7% on renewal energy arm stake sale buzz
Thermax is negotiating the sale of a controlling 51% stake in its renewable subsidiary, First Energy, at an enterprise value of 3,000 crore rupees. Divesting this capital-intensive asset frees the parent company balance sheet from project debt and developer capex, lifting return on equity. The transaction shifts Thermax toward higher-margin, capital-light engineering operations while generating cash for industrial decarbonisation projects.

Info Edge shares jump over 4% on Q2 biz update; billings rise 12.8% YoY
Standalone billings reached ₹822.3 crore, up 12.8 percent year-on-year for the second quarter. Because billings lead recognized revenue in subscription models, the pickup indicates stabilizing cash flows in the core recruitment portal Naukri, alongside steady momentum in 99acres. Sector-wise attrition and IT hiring figures in the upcoming quarterly results will confirm whether corporate tech hiring has genuinely bottomed.

AWL Agri’s growth metrics improve in Q2, but margins remain a pain point
Volume growth improved across branded foods and alternate channels, but edible oil volumes remained sluggish. Import duty increases and volatile global palm oil prices continue to compress refining margins, limiting EBITDA conversion despite revenue gains. Operating margins in the full quarterly filing will show whether price increases managed to offset raw material cost inflation across FMCG edible oil peers.

Fortis Healthcare, Apollo Hospitals, Max, Medanta shares rise: Should investors buy after 30% cancer drug price cap?
The government capped trade margins on non-scheduled oncology drugs at 30 percent, lowering retail prices by up to 70 percent. In-house pharmacies contribute roughly 15 to 20 percent of institutional hospital revenue. While gross margins on cancer therapies will compress, chains such as Apollo, Max, and Fortis typically offset pharmacy margin caps through upward revisions in bed charges and procedure tariffs.

The distribution acts as the primary cash transfer mechanism to service maturing offshore debt at parent entity Vedanta Resources. High dividend yields support parent solvency but constrain domestic capital expenditure across zinc, aluminium, and oil assets ahead of the planned corporate reorganization.

Demergers can narrow the holding company discount by attracting sector-focused institutional capital, but debt allocation across each newly formed unit will determine individual post-listing equity multiples. Filings detailing debt apportionment among the spun-off entities will clarify fair value.

Soaring freight rates threaten Asia's appetite for US crude
Surging supertanker freight rates on the transatlantic route have made delivered United States crude significantly more expensive for Asian refiners. Higher shipping costs reduce the arbitrage window for long-haul barrels, prompting Indian refiners like Indian Oil, BPCL, and Reliance to replace American grades with shorter-haul Middle Eastern and Russian crudes. Monthly crude import slates from the petroleum ministry will show the resulting procurement shift.

China to resume October fuel exports after holiday pause, sources say
Chinese state refiners will resume diesel and gasoline exports this month following a holiday pause, adding product supply to the Asian market. Increased regional fuel availability caps Singapore refining cracks, which directly pressures gross refining margins for Indian processors such as Reliance Industries, IOCL, and BPCL. A drop in diesel crack spreads below $15 a barrel in upcoming Singapore benchmark data would confirm sustained margin pressure.
